prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the room into a near foreground—hands, arms, and the dark-clothed person roughly 0.1–0.8 m from the camera—and a background of furniture, doorway, wall, and tree roughly 2–5 m away; brighter regions indicate nearer surfaces. Across frames 1–2 the person’s lower body fills the centre/right foreground, frame 3 opens onto the room while the camera wearer’s hands remain close, frame 4 again contains a very near body or limb across the centre, and frame 5 restores a clearer distant-room view. It reveals proximity and occlusion more clearly than RGB, especially that the foreground person or limb blocks much of the room and that doorway figures are several metres behind it, but it does not reliably distinguish people from objects or indicate facing direction and eye contact. Depth boundaries are blurred and some similarly distant surfaces have inconsistent brightness, so metre estimates, contact distances, and separations between overlapping limbs are approximate.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies large person regions in frames 1–2 and 4 at approximately 0.2–1 m, plus smaller people around the doorway or far side of the room at roughly 3–5 m; it also marks isolated objects including a chair, bottle, TV, oven, and possible cell phone. The dominant nearby person shifts from the centre in frame 1 to the right in frame 2, disappears or becomes fragmented in frame 3, occupies the centre-right foreground in frame 4, and is mostly out of view in frame 5, while the smaller background detections remain separated by several metres. Unlike RGB, the masks make some overlaps explicit—for example, near person regions occlude furniture and distant people—and show which detected objects lie left, right, above, or behind those regions, but they provide no dependable metric depth, facing direction, gaze, or arm-reach information without comparison to RGB and depth. Several masks and labels appear unreliable: foreground hands or clothing are merged into person shapes, some people are only tiny fragments, and labels such as cell phone, TV, oven, bottle, and chair do not consistently match clearly visible RGB boundaries.
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains only one usable magenta hand skeleton, in frame 2 near the centre-left, corresponding to a hand approximately 0.3–0.7 m from the camera and extending rightward toward the nearby dark-clothed person or limb. Its joint trace clarifies the hand’s articulated shape and relative finger positions, which are difficult to separate in the blurred and partly occluded RGB foreground. No body skeletons and no reliable poses appear in frames 1, 3, 4, or 5, so this map cannot establish the room layout, distances between people, body facing direction, gaze, approach or retreat, or whether other objects are within anyone’s reach. The missing detections are especially unreliable because multiple people or limbs are visible in RGB and segmentation, yet almost all are absent from the pose output.
